Compute hospital-level injury severity measures

Source: R/iss.R
run_iss.Rd

ICD-9 diagnoses are scored with icdpicr; ICD-10 diagnoses are scored with an isolated adapter for the icdpicr2 2.1 API (2.1.0 or later). Diagnoses are scored once per hospital admission and then projected to optional ICU identifiers. Admissions without an ICU remain present. Ambiguous eICU ICD versions are excluded and represented by iss_status rather than inferred by regex.

Usage

run_iss(
  src_name,
  db_name = NULL,
  base_dir = NULL,
  con = NULL,
  icd_adjudication_path = NULL,
  publish = TRUE,
  enrichment = NULL
)

Arguments

src_name

Source name (for example, "mimic_iii_demo").

db_name

Optional Postgres database name.

base_dir

Project root. Defaults to getwd().

con

Optional explicit DBI connection.

icd_adjudication_path

Optional reviewed eICU ICD-version crosswalk.

publish

Whether to transactionally publish the result.

enrichment

Optional overrides from enrichment_options() or a named list.

Value

Invisibly returns the ISS data frame.

Details

Both scorers run on every admission, and the reported iss/niss/maxais are the element-wise maximum of the two: when an admission has both an ICD-9 and an ICD-10 scoring the higher value is reported, and when it has only one that one is reported. mechmaj/mechmin/intent are categorical and cannot be maximised, so they take the ICD-9 value when present and the ICD-10 value otherwise. The per-version columns (*_icd9, *_i10) are always published alongside, so either scoring can be recovered or compared.

maxais is the highest known AIS (1-6) across the two scorings. AIS 9 - "injury present, severity not specified" - is never treated as a severity: it cannot outrank a known AIS, and an admission whose injuries all have unknown severity gets maxais, iss and niss as NA with iss_status = "severity_unknown", distinct from "no_mapped_condition" (no code maps to an injury; scores reported as 0). The per-version columns keep the scorers' raw values, including 9.

This is deliberately a maximum and not a per-admission choice of coding system. It matters most for eICU, which codes the same stay in both systems (93.6% of stays in the reference SCID cohort carry both, at a median 50/50 split), so the two scorings are two representations of the same clinical content rather than two eras; taking the maximum keeps an injury that is documented in only one of them.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
run_iss("mimic_iv_demo", db_name = "rendehr")
} # }
